# Repository-wide GitHub Copilot instructions

This is an **AIIMS NORCET + HP Staff Nurse nursing study repository**. Before creating/editing any nursing content, always consult:

**[.github/skills/norcet-staff-nurse-github-publisher/SKILL.md](skills/norcet-staff-nurse-github-publisher/SKILL.md)**

Follow the complete publishing checklist there. Highlights:

1. Only **actually studied** topics; consolidate **2–4 related topics per long file**. Keep chapter → Concepts/MCQs/Previous-Year-Questions/Revision/Assets structure flat.
2. Medical concepts and reasoning in easy **Hinglish**; medical terms English. **ALL MCQ stems and A/B/C/D options unchanged English**. Answer explanations and exam memory tricks in Hinglish.
3. Label **every MCQ Easy / Medium / Difficult**; use challenging but syllabus-relevant NORCET and HP Staff Nurse items, with detailed elimination of other options.
4. Search official notices, authoritative medicine/nursing, relevant coaching pages, **specific YouTube teaching and YouTube MCQ-solution videos**. Verify video URLs; add both resource columns in chapter/topic navigation.
5. Keep **Previous Year Questions** distinct, accurately source-labeled, source-quoted only when permissible. Don't misrepresent memory-based questions as official verbatim papers.
6. Add original accurate diagrams/animations where useful, links between every Concepts/MCQs/Previous Year Questions page, references and verification.
7. On "push this to GitHub", perform actual GitHub edits and verify commit and links. Never fabricate publishing success.


8. On any push, audit completed topics for high-yield gaps; if justified, create **one cumulative extra combined `Concepts/Extra-High-Yield-Concepts-and-MCQs.md` file** with easy Hinglish supplementary concepts, **30+ unique nonduplicated English MCQs**, each answer hidden in a GitHub `<details>` dropdown with detailed Hinglish reasoning and helpful original diagrams. No filler, no unrelated advanced subjects; if 30 distinct questions are unavailable, do not force a file.

If older files contradict this skill, follow the skill and update the conflicting text.

9. **Resume, don't restart:** if learner returns to an earlier topic or sends multiple pushes on the same day, update the matching existing chapter/day files and preserve exact solved English MCQs. New original practice should favor Medium/Difficult application questions. Search source-backed previous papers from across India and relevant topic-specific teaching/MCQ videos. The Cardiovascular chapter is a placeholder until studied.

## Mandatory repository-wide conversational Roman Hinglish and complete-sentence retrofit — learner instruction, 28 November 2026

This is a binding language and teaching-quality gate for ALL existing and new chapters, all publishing, audit, explanation, metadata and website jobs, and all manual sessions. Use the Respiratory System concept notes as the learner-approved style benchmark, particularly `Chapters/Respiratory-System/Concepts/Day-01-Complete-Respiratory-Anatomy-Physiology.md`. Do not copy its medical content into unrelated chapters.

- Teach as if a friendly nursing teacher is explaining to a fresher in a real one-to-one conversation. Use simple everyday Roman Hindi mixed naturally with familiar English words, not Devanagari, stiff textbook English, literal translations or unexplained jargon. Retain necessary English medical terms and explain their meaning in ordinary words when first introduced. Explain the actual concept, not merely its definition.
- Use full, natural, grammatically complete sentences in every explanatory paragraph, bullet, numbered step and explanatory table cell. Include the subject, action and necessary reasoning. Prefer short connected paragraphs, one clear thought at a time. Use natural transitions such as "jab", "toh", "kyunki", "isliye" and "iska matlab hai". No disconnected pointers, sentence fragments, lists of keywords, arrow-only explanations or telegraphic notes as a substitute for teaching. Headings, navigation link labels, formulas, diagram labels, source titles, data values and brief memory aids may remain compact when supported by a full explanation elsewhere.
- For concepts, explain what it means, how normal physiology works, what changes and why, what the patient may experience, how assessment findings relate to the mechanism, what the nurse should do and why, and relevant precautions or escalation. Use practical examples and simple analogies where useful without distorting clinical facts. Do not remove medical depth, clinical distinctions, safety context or exam-level reasoning simply to make language easier.
- Apply this throughout Concepts, chapter README and every learner-facing index, topic introductions, revision, clinical examples, nursing management, embedded question explanations, MCQs, mock tests, PYQs, imported practice and website-rendered study explanations. Navigation prose and learner instructions must also be natural complete Hinglish sentences. Keep standard English medical headings, source titles and functional link labels where useful. Do not translate or rewrite English MCQ stems or any A/B/C/D options, exact historical question wording, answer keys, identifiers or evidence metadata merely for style.
- Every MCQ answer must remain hidden in its existing Markdown details block, with the correct option and a detailed natural Roman Hinglish explanation of why it is correct, plus a separate detailed explanation for EACH of the three incorrect options. Explain the relevant mechanism or decision and why the distractor does not fit the question. Where helpful, explain when the distractor would be appropriate and how to distinguish it in an exam. One-word verdicts, "wrong because incorrect", restating an option, shorthand and fragments do not pass. Add a useful exam clue in a complete sentence where appropriate. Keep difficulty, priority, provenance, verified clinical references and dedicated MCQ video evidence or explicit gaps.
- Example of unacceptable prose: "Alveolar inflammation. Fluid accumulation. Impaired gas exchange. Hypoxia." Required style: "Hamare lungs ke andar chhoti-chhoti hawa ki thailiyan hoti hain, jinhe alveoli kehte hain. Jab pneumonia ki wajah se inmein inflammation hota hai, toh fluid jama ho sakta hai. Is wajah se oxygen ko blood tak pahunchne mein dikkat ho sakti hai. Isliye nurse patient ki breathing aur oxygen saturation check karti hai." The example illustrates style, not a complete disease lesson.
- Retrospective correction is mandatory, not only a rule for new files. Work chapter by chapter in the existing curriculum order, resume from a verified file-level checkpoint and coordinate with the responsible owner before editing claimed scopes. Each owner should apply the standard to its existing and new content within its authorized scope. Audit all learner-facing Markdown files and record separately which concept/index/revision files and which numbered question explanations have been actually reviewed and repaired. Read explanations as if teaching aloud. A sample check, language detector, introductory paragraph or rule-file update alone does not certify a file or chapter. Retain existing audit requirements and record outstanding gaps honestly.
- Style-only corrections must preserve English stems/options, correct answers, question numbers, anchors, attempt history, counts, links, images, diagrams, hidden blocks, source evidence and other jobs' changes. If a clinical defect is found, verify it independently and use the existing corrective audit procedure. Never bulk-translate questions, inflate inventories, regenerate entire banks, force-push, or overwrite another owner's work. Follow all claim, checkpoint and safe publication rules, verify exact remote readback, and continue from the first incomplete file. Never mark the whole repository complete until every chapter's applicable material has actually passed the audit. Do not use semicolon punctuation in newly authored learner-facing prose, while preserving original questions, URLs and technical syntax.

## Latest learner correction — content-first creation, 28 November 2026

For forward content-creation sessions, prioritize actual new question authorship and commits rather than repeated retrospective audits. Select the lowest actual MCQ, mock and PYQ coverage among unclaimed priority chapters after checking current claims, chapter files, recent activity and open/draft PRs, including planned workstreams. Never interrupt another owner or regenerate a staged bank. Finish one selected chapter before advancing. Preserve all five hourly automations and the separate audit jobs. This correction changes sequencing, not clinical accuracy, evidence integrity or safe publication requirements.

- Author 20 genuinely distinct original questions per meaningful topic, targeting five topics and 100 originals per run. A finished 20-question bank should not wait merely for an earlier 30–40 target. Preserve higher established totals. Prioritize HP staff nurse/HPRCA/HPSSC and NORCET/AIIMS/PGIMER exam-standard questions, with a useful mix of explicit Easy, Medium and Difficult labels and realistic clinical application. Keep four plausible English options, hidden answers, four individual detailed conversational Roman Hinglish rationales, exam clues, priority and honest source metadata. Research authoritative clinical sources while writing.
- Complete topic-wise MCQ banks first, then ten chapter-only original-exclusive mocks of 120 questions each, targeting two complete tests per run, then source-traced previous-year practice mapped to its actual topic. Include AIIMS NORCET, PGIMER, HPRCA/HPSSC, military and other state/central staff nurse exams. Keep verified historical evidence separate from original practice and label adaptations and recalls honestly.
- Perform concise incremental checks of the NEW content for clinical correctness, distinct objectives, four-option/key alignment, format and sources while authoring. Do not repeat unchanged historical audits, run audit-only content sessions or block creation on retrospective review. Dedicated audit jobs retain their responsibilities. If an independent review or shared navigation release gate is outstanding, record it once and continue isolated new content commits where ownership allows. Do not bypass mandatory integration checks or count drafts as live.
- Put content in descriptive chapter-local MCQs, Mock-Tests and Previous-Year-Questions files, preserving existing IDs, learner history, claims and current chapter structure. Commit finished batches safely, verify exact remote readbacks, report new committed and live counts separately and record the next unfinished topic. Release only your own claim. Continue the same chapter next run. No force pushes, invented sources, duplicate questions or unsupported completion claims.

## Latest learner rule — repository-wide Easy/Medium balancing (28 November 2026)

This rule applies to all chapters, manual sessions and publishing lanes and supersedes earlier preferences for predominantly Medium/Difficult or harder new practice. Existing clinical, ownership, provenance, original-only mock, learner-history and safe-release rules remain binding. Preserve all five hourly automations and separate audit responsibilities.

- Target approximately one-third each Easy, Medium and Difficult among completed topic-bank originals. Easy means foundational recall or routine nursing knowledge, Medium means straightforward nursing application, common clinical scenarios or calculations, and Difficult means syllabus-relevant multi-step clinical reasoning. Never use obscurity or specialist-level material merely to raise difficulty. The distribution is a learner-selected practice target, not an official examination quota. Research against INC curriculum and AIIMS NORCET, HPRCA/HPSSC HP staff nurse and other Indian state/central staff nurse exam scope.
- For the dedicated balancing lane, begin at the first chapter in the existing curriculum index (Nursing Foundations), work topic by topic in order, temporarily defer claimed or overlapping scopes and revisit them before declaring completion. Count existing labels per meaningful topic as a brief incremental check, not a retrospective audit. Add only genuinely new Easy and Medium questions during the balancing phase, ordinarily 5–6 per deficient topic per pass and up to 100 per run. Allocate by actual deficits, not a fixed 50/50 split. Aim for 15–20 distinct originals per topic where appropriate (15 = 5/5/5, 18 = 6/6/6, 20 = 7/7/6). Seven of each is 21. Preserve larger existing banks and higher established targets, and add beyond the initial target where needed to correct imbalance. Do not delete, relabel without evidence, or duplicate existing questions to force ratios. Record outstanding deficits honestly, including topics needing Difficult items later.
- All new complete 120-question chapter mocks must contain exactly 40 Easy, 40 Medium and 40 Difficult independently authored mock-exclusive questions. During Easy/Medium balancing, author only the deficient Easy/Medium portions and keep incomplete mocks staged, unless sufficient distinct Difficult mock-exclusive questions are already available for that same test. Never reuse topic-bank questions or other mocks. Preserve published mock identities, scoring, attempts and history. Balance legacy mocks through safe separately coordinated additions or successor tests rather than silently changing completed attempts.
- Keep English stems and four English options, visible difficulty and priority, honest original-practice provenance, hidden correct answer, four individual full-sentence conversational Roman Hinglish rationales, exam clue and specific verified authoritative references. Retain dedicated MCQ-practice video evidence or explicitly record gaps. Compare new stems and substantive learning objectives against existing banks, concepts, mocks, PYQs and overlapping staged PRs. Check current claims and reserve exclusive scope before writing. Do not repeat historical audits in the content lane. Commit actual validated content in chapter-local packages, verify exact remote readbacks, distinguish staged from live, record counts by difficulty and next unfinished topic, and release only your own claim. Independent review and mandatory publication gates still apply.

## Latest learner rule — balanced content batches and evidence-weighted topic depth (28 November 2026)

- For normal content creation, target five complete 20-question topic banks per run, 100 distinct originals overall. Distribute Easy, Medium and Difficult as evenly as possible: 6/7/7 per bank with the smaller category rotated, and 33/33/34 per 100 with the extra category rotated. These are practice targets, not official examination quotas. Correct existing chapter deficits through distinct additions and retain the dedicated Easy/Medium balancing lane's deficit-led exception. Do not delete prior questions or relabel them without evidence. Every new 120-question original-exclusive mock must contain exactly 40 of each difficulty. Complete ten mocks per chapter, normally two per run, after topic banks are complete and before the remaining topic-mapped historical question phase.
- Twenty originals per meaningful topic is a baseline, never a cap. Preserve higher established totals. Allocate additional questions to demonstrably high-yield topics, not to trivial subdivisions. Use accessible actual papers and answer keys from AIIMS NORCET, PGIMER/SGPGI, HPRCA/HPSSC, military nursing and other Indian state/central staff nurse recruitment. Log exam, year/shift when evidenced, item/page locator, source URL, topic mapping and sample coverage. Deduplicate repeated papers and distinguish verified items from coaching recalls. Use observed item counts with the denominator of accessible papers or questions and explicitly label incomplete samples. Where frequency is not established, describe the priority as curriculum/clinical judgment rather than historical frequency.
- Research accessible nursing books, PDFs, coaching websites and topic-specific YouTube practice sessions for concepts and exam patterns. Verify clinical keys against current authoritative guidance. Write independent English stems and plausible options with hidden answers, four separate conversational Roman Hinglish rationales, exam clues and honest provenance. Do not reproduce protected banks in bulk, invent source metadata or call an original item a PYQ. Preserve source/evidence gaps rather than inventing facts. Maintain exclusive chapter ownership, sibling semantic screening, exact remote readbacks, independent review and release gates. All five hourly jobs, learner history and concurrent sessions remain untouched.
